vendor-id.description: Optional upstream vendor/account group id such as anthropic, google, openai, or openrouter. Distinct from the harness provider id.

connector-options.description: Free-form per-connector parameters (RV323). No per-connector sub-schema at v1 — known/required keys per verified connector are documented in PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_REFERENCE/endpoints/provider-model-endpoints.md, not enforced here.

api-key-ref.description: Secret reference (e.g. env:VAR_NAME), never a literal credential.

model-discovery.description: remote-account only: what AUDiaGentic knows about the source's models. Not applicable to local-endpoint, whose one model is fully declared inline.

model-filter.description: remote-account only. Include/exclude glob patterns applied to custom-entries projection and AG-side alias exposure. Does NOT constrain native key injection, which always enables the full vendor/aggregator model set.

model-id.description: local-endpoint only: the single model this source declares.

provider-overrides.description: Per-AUDiaGentic-provider-id rendering overrides (not upstream model-vendor ids — see arch-standards §1 terminology note).

default.description: True marks this source's model as the default selection when a job/profile omits an explicit model.

resource-id.description: AS105/AS101: local-endpoint only. Groups sources that share one physical/compute resource (e.g. multiple models behind one llama-swap host, or the same model loaded on two GPUs). Sources sharing a resource-id contend for that resource's capacity; a swap-capable resource cannot run two different resource-id-sharing sources' models at once. Machine-wide fact -- expected to be declared at the user-global config tier, not per-project, since the resource itself is shared infrastructure.

concurrency.description: AS105/AS101: local-endpoint only. Max concurrent requests this source's model can run when it is the active/loaded model on its resource-id. A larger model on the same hardware typically supports fewer concurrent sequences than a smaller one -- concurrency is per source, never a flat per-resource number.
